title: Operations Ecosystem Handbook: Access, Change, Data, Procurement, and Templates
author: Priya Shah
body:
Overview

Purpose: This handbook centralizes Redwood Inference’s company-wide operational policies for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and reusable internal templates. It provides consistent decision thresholds, owners, and step-by-step procedures teams must follow.

Scope: Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and approved vendors unless a separate customer contract or legal requirement overrides a default. Exceptions must be documented and approved via the Risk & Exceptions process.

Owners and escalation
- Primary owner: Finance & Legal (policy maintenance).
- Operational owners: Engineering (access provisioning & change review), Eng-SRE (production change approvals and runbooks), People Ops (travel and expense policies), Procurement (vendor onboarding and purchase approvals), Security (data classification and sensitive approvals).
- Escalation path: Team Lead -> Platform Security -> Director of Eng-SRE -> VP Finance -> Chief Legal Officer.

1) Access & Permissions
Intro: Access decisions balance speed and principle of least privilege. All access is logged and reviewed. Access requests and approvals must use the central Access Request system (Jira ticket prefix ACCESS-) unless an emergency process is invoked.

Key definitions
- Standard access: Non-privileged accounts, code repositories, and internal tools. Approval by team lead.
- Privileged access: Root, database admin, KMS/HSM operations, production SSH. Requires security review and a privileged access request.
- Emergency access: Short-term elevated access for critical incidents. Must be documented retroactively within 24 hours (see Emergency Access process).

SLAs and thresholds
- Standard requests: resolved in 3 business days (SLA).
- Privileged requests: resolved in 5 business days, security review required.
- Emergency requests: acknowledged within 1 hour, granted only when approved by on-call Eng-SRE and Platform Security.

Standard process (day-to-day)
1. Open ACCESS-<team>-<short-desc> ticket and select template (standard | privileged | emergency).
2. Attach justification, business owner, and requested duration.
3. Team lead + security approver approve via ticket workflow.
4. Provisioning performed by identity team or delegated approver.
5. Ticket automatically moves to access review queue after provisioning for periodic audit.

Emergency access process (incident-driven)
1. Pager duty alert -> engineer requests emergency access via Slack emergency channel and creates ACCESS-EMERG ticket within 1 hour.
2. On-call Eng-SRE + Platform Security must approve in Slack with reference to ticket id.
3. Access is granted with an expiration (default 4 hours).
4. Post-incident: engineer must provide root cause and list of commands executed in the ticket. Security performs retroactive audit within 72 hours.

Periodic reviews
- Quarterly: Team leads must certify all privileged accounts assigned to their teams.
- Annual: Org-level access review and remediation plan coordinated by Security.

2) Change Management
Intro: All changes that affect production availability, security posture, or billing/cost must follow the Change Process. The change categories below determine approval and testing requirements. Use CHG- prefix in Jira.

Change categories and requirements
- Standard change (low risk): Non-prod config updates, documentation, minor infra changes. Require peer review and automated CI checks. Can be scheduled without further approvals.
- Significant change (medium risk): Deployments to production affecting >5% of traffic or changes to model serving config (batch sizes, KV cache behavior). Require canary rollout plan, owner sign-off, SLO impact analysis, and Ops reviewer.
- Major change (high risk): Migrations, database schema changes, KMS rotations, network or IAM redesigns. Require formal RFC, impact analysis, test plan, rollback plan, and Director-level approval.
- Emergency change: Patches required to restore service. Emergency changes allowed only during incident with on-call approval and must be documented and post-reviewed.

Mandatory artifacts for Significant & Major changes
- Change RFC (short): Purpose, owners, impact scope, rollback plan, test matrices, runbook steps.
- Canary plan: Traffic percentage schedule, monitoring windows (min 30 minutes), success/failure criteria mapped to SLOs.
- Rollback trigger conditions: latency increase >25% vs baseline for 3 consecutive sampling windows, token error rate increase >2x, or customer-impacting 5xx spike.

Change approval cadence and SLAs
- Standard: peer review and automated checks; deploy in next scheduled window.
- Significant: 48-hour review window; schedule deploy in next maintenance window.
- Major: minimum 7-business-day review and Exec sign-off.
- Emergency: retro-review within 72 hours; change ticket must contain executed commands and postmortem linkage.

3) Data Management and Retention
Intro: Data classification and retention must meet legal, security, and product needs. Follow the Data Classification Matrix and retention baseline below. For any contract-specific retention, legal overrides the baseline.

Classification (examples)
- Public: Docs intended for public consumption.
- Internal: Non-sensitive internal docs, logs with no PII.
- Confidential: Business sensitive, performance dashboards with customer identifiers.
- Sensitive/PII: Customer personal data, secrets, private keys.

Retention baseline table
- Application logs (non-PII): 90 days.
- Metrics & observability raw data: 365 days aggregated (retention at the raw sample level 90 days).
- Crash reports and incident recordings: 365 days.
- Customer PII: default retention 2 years after last active transaction or contract termination unless legal requires a different period.
- Audit logs (security, IAM): 7 years (retention required for compliance audits).

Data access and handling rules
- PII access must be restricted to named roles and require privileged access ticket.
- Encryption: data at rest encrypted with KMS-managed keys; customer keys may be used in Private deployments.
- Backups: daily backups for production databases with 30-day rolling retention, longer where contracts require.

Delete and retention processes
1. Data owners file a Data Deletion Request (DDR-<product>) with scope and query.
2. Legal reviews for contractual obligations.
3. Engineering executes deletion scripts in a sandbox environment and provides proof-of-delete report.
4. Production deletion executed during maintenance window and verified by Security.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Intro: Procurement protects Redwood’s financial commitments and enables predictable vendor management. The Procurement team manages vendor contracts, POs, and payment approvals. Employee-level expenses follow the People Ops expense policy.

Approval thresholds
- <$5,000: Team lead approval (submit PRQ ticket).
- $5,000–$50,000: Procurement and Finance approval required.
- >$50,000 or multi-year commitments: VP-level approval and legal review.

Purchase steps for non-contracted buys
1. Create PRQ-<team>-<purpose> in procurement queue with justification, cost center, and vendor details.
2. Procurement evaluates vendor, validates pricing, and if needed requests vendor security questionnaire.
3. Finance issues PO after approvals.
4. Vendor onboarding (see Vendor Management checklist) prior to going-live.

Expense policy highlights (employee reimbursements)
- Reimbursable timeframe: submit within 60 days of expense date.
- Meal per diem: domestic $70/day; international per diem follows government guidance and must be pre-approved.
- Lodging: reasonable economy/business class for customer meetings; upgrades require justification and Director approval.
- Personal expenses will be denied (e.g., minibar charges).

Procurement SLA targets
- Standard requests under $5k: 5 business days.
- $5k–$50k: 10–15 business days depending on vendor response.
- >$50k: variable; procurement will provide an estimated timeline within 3 business days.

5) Vendor Management
Intro: Vendors that access Redwood systems or customer data must go through Vendor Risk and Onboarding. The goal is to reduce operational, security, and contractual risk.

Onboarding checklist (minimum)
- Completed Vendor Intake form with contract term, contact points, and scope.
- Security questionnaire (SIG or equivalent) completed and scored by Security.
- Contract with liability clauses and data processing addendum (DPA) where applicable.
- SLA definitions: uptime targets, support windows, escalation contacts, and scheduled maintenance windows.
- Access model: least privilege, time-bound credentials, and visibility in vendor inventory.

Vendor SLA & KPIs (recommended defaults)
- Availability: 99.9% monthly for core infra vendors; for non-critical SaaS, negotiable.
- Response: 4-hour acknowledgement for Severity-1 incidents; 24-hour initial response for Severity-3.
- Security: annual penetration test report or SOC2 Type II preferred for vendors handling PII.

Periodic review and offboarding
- Quarterly: procurement tracks vendor spend and risk flags.
- Annual: security re-evaluation for vendors with access to PII.
- Offboarding steps: revoke credentials, certify data returns or deletion, and close vendor record in procurement system.

6) Travel and Remote Work Expenses
Intro: Travel must align with business need and minimize cost. People Ops approves travel and maintains travel booking partners.

Pre-approval and timelines
- Domestic travel: team lead approval at least 5 business days before travel.
- International travel: People Ops and manager approval at least 15 business days before travel (visa timelines may require more lead time).

Airfare and lodging guidance
- Air: economy or basic economy for flights under 6 hours; premium economy or coach-plus for flights over 6 hours with Director pre-approval for upgrades.
- Hotel: business-standard hotels; avoid extended-stay unless meeting multi-day onsite requirements.

Safety and duty of care
- People Ops maintains emergency contact lists and travel insurance guidance.
- Employees traveling to regions with security advisories must register with People Ops and receive manager approval.

7) Templates and Reusable Artifacts
Intro: Below are the canonical templates teams must use. These reduce review friction and ensure consistent evidence for audits. Each template is available in the central Templates library (link in related pages).

Access Request (sample fields)
- Title: ACCESS-<team>-<purpose>
- Requester: name + employee id
- Business owner: name + team
- Access type: standard | privileged | emergency
- Resources requested: list with exact identifiers (e.g., vault://secrets/production)
- Duration: start and end date (default 90 days for privileged)
- Justification: business impact if denied

Change Request RFC (short)
- Title and owner
- Summary of change
- Impacted services and customer impact
- Test plan and rollback steps
- Canary schedule and success metrics
- Approval checklist (peer, ops, security, legal if applicable)

Vendor Onboarding Checklist (sample)
- Intake form link: [procurement intake]
- Security questionnaire: attached
- Contract signed: yes/no
- PO created: yes/no
- Access assigned: list resources and expiration
- SLA recorded in vendor portal: yes/no

Expense Reimbursement Form (required fields)
- Employee name, ID, cost center
- Date(s) of expense
- Merchant and expense category (travel/meal/lodging/supplies)
- Amount and currency
- Receipt attachment (required for >$25)
- Approval chain (manager, finance)

8) Audit, Exceptions, and Continuous Improvement
- Exceptions: submit Risk Exception Form with justification; CFO + Security approve exceptions >90 days. All exceptions must have a renewal date.
- Audits: Procurement, Security, and Finance coordinate annual internal audits. Audit findings get tracked in the Audit Tracker and assigned remediation owners.
- Continuous improvement: A cross-functional Ops Review committee meets monthly to triage policy gaps, implement improvements, and publish quarterly updates to this handbook.

Quick reference table (decision thresholds)
- Access standard SLA: 3 business days | privileged SLA: 5 business days | emergency: 1 hour
- Procurement approval: < $5k team lead | $5k–$50k procurement+finance | >$50k VP+legal
- Change review: standard (peer), significant (48 hours), major (7 business days)
- Data retention baseline: logs 90d | metrics aggregated 365d | audit logs 7y | customer PII default 2y

Contact and support
- Primary policy contact: finance-policy@redwood.com
- Procurement queue: prq@redwood.com (PRQ- prefix in Jira)
- Access requests: access-requests@redwood.com (ACCESS- prefix)
- Security escalations: security-oncall@pager.redwood.com

Appendix: Example CLI snippets
- Create a privileged access ticket (example):
  curl -X POST https://jira.redwood.internal/rest/api/2/issue -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"fields": {"project":{"key":"ACCESS"}, "summary":"Request privileged DB access - analytics", "issuetype":{"name":"Task"}, "description":"Requester: Priya Shah\\nBusiness owner: Marcus Leung\\nResources: db-prod.redwood:analytics\\nDuration: 90 days"}}'

- Sample deletion proof-of-delete output (format):
  deleted_records: 12345
  query: "DELETE FROM events WHERE created_at < '2023-01-01' AND team = 'alpha'"
  executed_by: automation-deleter-02
  timestamp: 2025-09-12T02:34:00Z

Revision history
- 2025-06-12 (Priya Shah): Initial draft and baseline thresholds published.
- 2025-10-04 (Marcus Leung): Added Emergency Access flow and tightened privileged request SLA.
- 2026-02-18 (Priya Shah): Updated procurement thresholds and travel per diem rates; clarified data retention baseline.

End of document
